questions.question:
[Extract Context: "“Since you have been so nice to me a ll day long, as if I wa s a captain, I want 
to be nice to you, in return, as if I was a real captain — for I do not want you 
to be embarrassed at this Christmas season by a thief; but you can give back 
the mone..."]

Which of the following CANNOT be attributed to the peddler, according to the 
above extract?
options: indebtedness
reform
self-pity
self-awareness
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Answer Key: Option (B).

Why did the peddler gift a rattrap as a Christmas present?
options:
It was all the peddler had that he could give away, and represented his 
turn to honesty.

It symbolized his successful escape from entrapment as he returned the 
stolen money.

It served as a remi nder for Edla to be war y of the dangerous te mptations 
of the world.

It was a practical and convenient present that the lady of the house could 
effectively use.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Answer Key: Option (C).

options: Option (i)
Option (ii)
Option (iii)

questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (B).

questions.question:
“Left to his own meditations”, one day the peddler fell into “a line of thought, 
which really seemed to him entertaining”. What d oes the peddler’s 
conception of the world as a rattrap, signify about him?
options: The peddler had a lot of time on his hands, with nothing much to do.

The peddle r was a reflective man whose wisdom did not depend on his 
status.
The peddler was a lonely vagrant trying to make sense of his fortunes.
The peddler was a rattrap seller, and his work deeply inspired him.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (C).

questions.question:
“Yes, that was a fine fellow you let into the house,” said her father.
What light does the given line throw on the ironmaster as a father?
options: The ironmaster was disapproving of Edla’s decision to let the peddler stay.
The ironmaster blamed his daughter for harbouring a criminal at home.
The ironmaster was being playful with Edla, and supported her decisions.
The ironmaster loved Edla but thought her to be too naïve and idealistic.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (A).

questions.question:
Though the reader does not meet C aptain von Stahle in pe rson, they 
encounter the captain symbolically. How?
options:
The ironmaster misidentifies the peddler as his old friend, the Captain and 
invites him home.

The reader realizes the peddler is actually Captain vo n Stahle when he 
signs off the letter.

Edla at tends to the peddler as respectfully, caring ly and kindly, as she 
would have the Captain.

The peddler accepts the error of his ways, and displays the qualities 
expected of a Captain.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (D).
